title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: Suppose that \(13\) cards numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(13\) are arranged in a row. The task is to pick them up in numerically increasing order, working repeatedly from left to right. In the example below, cards \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3\) are picked up on the first pass, \(4\) and \(5\) on the second pass, \(6\) on the third pass, \(7,\) \(8,\) \(9,\) \(10\) on the fourth pass, and \(11,\) \(12,\) \(13\) on the fifth pass. For how many of the \(13!\) possible orderings of the cards will the \(13\) cards be picked up in exactly two passes?

solutions.text:
Let \(\text{pos}(k)\) be the position of card \(k.\) A fresh pass is needed exactly when \(\text{pos}(k+1)\lt\text{pos}(k),\) so the number of passes is one more than the number of descents in the sequence \(\text{pos}(1),\text{pos}(2),\ldots,\text{pos}(13).\)

To build a permutation with at most one descent, choose the entries before the possible descent and write both chosen blocks in increasing order. There are \(2^{13}\) subsets. The \(14\) initial segments \(\varnothing,\{1\},\ldots,\{1,\ldots,13\}\) produce no descent; every other subset produces a unique permutation with one descent. Hence the count is \(2^{13}-14=8178.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: A new pass begins exactly when the next number to pick up lies to the left of the previous one
Two passes means the sequence of positions \(\text{pos}(1),\ldots,\text{pos}(13)\) has exactly one descent
